label: NAP 16-port
notes: Sixteen drop ports, the feeder entry that feeds them and a fourth tray, so 17 cable ports and 48 splice positions. `ports` is the cable count the engine checks: engine/network.js warns when the spans touching a closure outnumber its `ports` (docs/PARTS.md states the same), so the field is drop adapters PLUS the feeder entry, never the adapter count alone. It said 16 until 2026-11-27, so a fully loaded 16-drop NAP with its feeder read '17 cables into 16 ports'. Vendor boxes publish the two counts separately - CommScope's SSC2811-SM-8 '1(Input) + 8(Drop)', Prysmian's MTWB '16 drop ports' against 'No. of Input cable ports 1 top and 1 bottom' - and this row's extra entry over nap-8's is what a cascaded site spends when the feeder carries on to the next box. Ports, trays and splice capacity are typical of the class rather than one datasheet (IEC 61753-1 qualifies the closure and publishes no capacity figure). Replace with the bought closure's datasheet before ordering.
